function: Two-stage residual DNN predicts analog and digital precoders and combiners jointly for multi-user partially connected hybrid MIMO, balancing spectral and energy efficiency (pp. 1-2).
system: mmWave massive MIMO, partially connected hybrid: 144 UPA transmit antennas, 4 RF chains (p. 7), 4 users with 4 antennas, no RIS, carrier not given (pp. 2, 6).
method: Residual DNN (FC layers, 1-D convolutional residual modules), analog and digital stages; unsupervised learning with exponential SE loss, Adam, 500 iterations (pp. 4-6).
data_channel: Own Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave generator (5 clusters, 10 rays, UPA, Rayleigh gains); training CSI noise 5-20 dB; no standard model or dataset (pp. 3, 5-6).
test_conditions: 70/30 train/test split of generated noisy channels (5-20 dB); SE and EE swept over SNR, NT, K, Pt, averaged over 100 realizations (pp. 5-8).
baselines: Non-learned: fully digital optimal, MMSE, BD-GMD-THP (fully connected), CA-HP, MU-SIC (partially connected); no learned baseline simulated (p. 6).
metrics: Spectral efficiency, energy efficiency (bits/Hz/J), complexity order, computation time over 100 channels (pp. 6-9).
complexity: Order O(max{CF NR NT, NT^2 NRF^2, ...}) in Table III; runtime 0.7930 s over 100 channels in Table IV (p. 9).
openness: none (no code or data link; channels from own simulator, p. 6).
q1_support: p. 6: "the mmWave channel adopts the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model, where Ncl = 5, Nray = 10" with Rayleigh gains (p. 3): a custom simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.901, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 6: "70% and 30% of the total data generated are selected as the training and testing data sets respectively" is a held-out part of the same data; the sweeps over SNR, NT, K and Pt (pp. 6-8) are not stated to test a model trained elsewhere, and the input size 2K NR NT (p. 6) changes with K and NT.
q3_support: p. 6: "the MMSE method [17], the FC structure-based BD-GMD-THP [30], the PC structure-based CA-HP [31] and MU-SIC approaches [32]" are all non-learned (MMSE is a matrix-inverse method, p. 9); the DL methods [18]-[23] appear only in related work (p. 2), so no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "the complexity of the proposed approach is of order" O(max{CF NR NT, NT^2 NRF^2, CF NRF NRF, Ns^2 NRF^2}) (Table III); p. 9: "Table IV shows the computation time taken via the different algorithms", proposed 0.7930 s.
q5_support: p. 6: "the proposed RTDNN framework is implemented and trained by PyCharm based on PyTorch" on channels from its own generator; no code or data link is given and no public dataset is used.
notes: Included in area 3 (hybrid precoder and combiner design for a multi-user mmWave MIMO link). Legends of Figs. 10-17 (pp. 6-8) list only Optimal, MMSE, BD-GMD-THP, CA-HP, MU-SIC and Proposed. The baseline named "the MMSE method [17]" cites a DNN paper, but p. 9 describes its cost as calculating an inverse matrix, so it is not counted as a learned baseline; reviewer to confirm. The sweeps over NT and K (Figs. 11-12, 15-16) are not stated to reuse one trained network, so q2 stays 0. Carrier frequency is not stated (mmWave only).
